papers.title: Laser Powder Bed Fusion of a Ti-16Nb-Based Alloy: Processability, Microstructure, and Mechanical Properties
papers.abstract: Titanium alloys, especially Ti6Al4V, are widely used in biomedical implants due to their biocompatibility and mechanical strength. However, their high elastic modulus (>100 GPa), compared to that of human bone (10–30 GPa), often causes stress shielding, reducing implant lifespan. To address this, titanium alloys with lower elastic modulus are under development. In this study, Ti-based multi-element alloy with 16 wt.% Nb samples were fabricated using laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) from a premixed powder blend of Ti6Al4V and Nb-Hf-Ti. Processing high-melting Nb-based alloys via L-PBF poses challenges, which were mitigated through optimized parameters, including a maximum laser power of 100 W. Eleven parameter sets were employed to evaluate printability, microstructure, and mechanical properties. Microstructural analysis revealed Widmanstätten structures composed of α and β phases, along with isolated spherical pores. Reduced hatch spacing and slower laser speed led to increased hardness. The highest hardness (~43 HRC) was observed at the highest energy density (266 J/mm3), while the lowest (~28 HRC) corresponded to 44 J/mm3. Elastic modulus values ranged from 30 to 35 GPa, closely matching that of bone. These results demonstrate the potential of the developed Ti-based alloy containing 16 wt.% Nb as a promising candidate for load-bearing biomedical implants.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该研究涉及Ti-16Nb合金而非Ti-6Al-4V，且未讨论股骨柄设计或力学性能，与方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper studies a Ti-16Nb alloy, not Ti-6Al-4V, and does not address femoral stem structural design, stress shielding, implant geometry, or any implant-level biomechanical analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 为解决Ti6Al4V弹性模量过高导致应力屏蔽的问题，开发低模量Ti-16Nb合金。
summary_zh.method: 使用激光粉末床熔融技术从预混粉末制备Ti-16Nb试样，优化工艺参数并表征显微组织和力学性能。
summary_zh.result: 获得Widmanstätten组织，弹性模量30-35 GPa，与骨匹配，硬度随能量密度变化。
summary_zh.validation: 通过显微组织观察和硬度、模量测试验证材料性能。

summary_en.motivation: To address stress shielding caused by the high elastic modulus of Ti6Al4V, a lower modulus Ti-16Nb alloy was developed for biomedical implants.
summary_en.method: Ti-16Nb samples were fabricated by laser powder bed fusion from a premixed powder blend, with optimized process parameters; microstructure and mechanical properties were characterized.
summary_en.result: Widmanstätten microstructure with α+β phases was obtained; elastic modulus ranged from 30 to 35 GPa, matching bone, and hardness varied with energy density.
summary_en.validation: Validation included microstructural analysis and mechanical testing (hardness and elastic modulus measurements).
